title: Understanding Bias-Variance Decomposition
text: Recall the bias-variance decomposition formula: E[(y-f(x))**2]=sigma**2+Var[f(x)]+(E[f(x)]-g(x))**2. Here, sigma is the standard deviation of the measurement errors, Var[f(x)] is the variance of the predictions, and (E[f(x)]-g(x))**2 is the squared bias.

title: Identify Given Values
text: From the problem, we know: $$sigma=4$$, preds $$mean=104.130417$$, preds $$std=8.255889$$, and MSE $$mean=101.930101$$. Use these values in the bias-variance decomposition formula.

title: Calculate Variance of Predictions
text: The variance of the predictions is the square of the standard deviation of the predictions. Calculate $$Var[f(x)]={8.255889}^2$$.

title: Calculate Squared Bias
text: Use the formula for MSE: MSE=sigma**2+Var[f(x)]+(E[f(x)]-g(x))**2. Rearrange to find the squared bias: (E[f(x)]-g(x))**2=MSE-sigma**2-Var[f(x)].

title: Compute Variance of Predictions
text: Calculate the variance of the predictions: $$Var[f(x)]={8.255889}^2$$.

title: Compute Squared Bias
text: Calculate the squared bias using the formula: (E[f(x)]-g(x))**2=101.930101-4**2-68.168.

title: Estimate Empirical Bias
text: The empirical bias is the square root of the squared bias. Calculate $$\sqrt{17.770101}$$.
